description: deixis-set-v1 conformance vectors, slot-member form, in the N[T] spelling: the profile of docs/design/0005-set-keys.md under ADR 0009, from 0005's section 'Under ADR 0009: the slot-member image is preserved exactly' as it stands at a0461d3. HISTORICAL under ADR 0010 (1a9bb6d), which makes node values mandatory: this file reads as deixis-set-v1 over Node[Option[U]], U being the member encoder's carrier. Every own value here is that option slot's none or some, ≈ respects the tag, the image and recognizer are the 0005 section above, and E is ADR 0010 §6's L[U] → Node[Option[U]], spelled as before. All 9 judgments hold in that reading: each case was re-judged on 2026-09-23, planted flips were reported as disagreements, and no judgment changed. No case judges containment, map or ADR 0009's absence-sensitive order. Hand-authored from that section alone, with set.json and ADR 0009 §10.1's embedding E for the preserved half. Not generated by an implementation, and replayed against the four cores by tools/conformance/harness.mjs. Written by the lane that did not write the section, under the independence rule 0005 states. Two parts. (1) The preserved half: one law BY REFERENCE per case kind of set.json, re-reading that file's verdicts through E. Their judgments are set.json's, already reviewed, not new ones, and each law pins the source counts it re-reads. (2) The two refusals that are new in N, valued_set_node and member_with_children. These are new judgments, each built from one accepted base (set.json's recognize-coherent through E, spelled out below) by exactly one change. Nodes use the N[T] spelling of NODE-PLAN.md, and own values are spelled per the case's member encoder, as set.json spells leaves: a hex string under `bytes`, {class, representation} under `class`. So under `bytes`, {"some": ""} is Some of the empty byte string, never None. Refusal reasons: mis_keyed, struct_member and leaf_node (carried), valued_set_node and member_with_children (new). Every refusal case has exactly one defect: 0005 fixes no precedence among reasons for a node with several, and set.json never needed one, so no such case is authored.

cases.name: set-json-recognize-through-embedding
cases.law: for every recognize case of the source: recognizing E(node) in N gives the case's `valid` and, when refused, the case's `reason`
cases.note: 0005: recognition is unchanged in substance, and each carried reason is restated so that an old refusal's image refuses for the same reason. mis_keyed is k ≠ e(x). struct_member is a child whose own value is None, the image of a Struct child. leaf_node is a set node Node(Some(x), ∅), the image of a bare Leaf. A replayer MUST refuse if the source's counts differ from those pinned here: such a change is an erratum to set.json, and this law must then be re-checked by a person, not silently re-run. The reason is part of the verdict. Before af2612c the harness checked only isSet for set.json's recognize cases, so those reasons had never been machine-checked. Since af2612c it replays them through this law, reasons included. FINDING against 0005's section, not against this file, taken in d1b5bd9: this law also settled a shape the section had left open. Node(Some(t), ∅) is exactly leaf_node's shape, and valued_set_node as first written, Node(Some(t), {coherent members}), also covered it when the member map was empty. recognize-leaf-node through E is that node and carries leaf_node, so valued_set_node has to mean at least one member, which the section now says.

cases.name: set-json-form-through-embedding
cases.law: for every form case of the source: building set(members) in N, from `members` in authored order, gives a node ≡ E(node), and that node recognizes as a set
cases.note: 0005's image is set(S) = Node(None, { e(x) ↦ Node(Some(x), ∅) | x ∈ S }). That is E(Struct({ e(x) ↦ Leaf(x) })), so building in N commutes with E and the old verdict carries. The empty set is Node(None, ∅), the image of Struct(∅) (form-empty-set).

cases.name: set-json-duplicate-through-embedding
cases.law: for every duplicate case of the source: building set(members) in N fails duplicate_key at the case's `key`
cases.note: Idempotence by construction belongs to the floor (0005: the floor already refuses duplicate keys), and ADR 0009 §3 keeps child keys unique, so the second insert still cannot be spelled. node-invalid.json refuses duplicate keys in N. Under `class`, ≈-equal members with different representations still spell one key.

cases.name: set-json-membership-through-embedding
cases.law: for every membership case of the source: in set(members) built in N, e(value) is a key of the set node exactly when the query's `in` is true
cases.note: 0005: membership is key membership, one lookup at e(q), and nothing in it depends on the node model. The lookup never reads a member's own value: membership-is-by-class asks with a representation that was never stored and expects IN.

cases.name: set-json-identity-through-embedding
cases.law: for every identity case of the source: E(left) ≡ E(right) in N, in both directions, exactly when the case's `equal` is true
cases.note: Set identity reduces to node identity (0004's transport law 3, which 0005's section keeps), and ADR 0009 §10.1 gives n ≡ m iff E(n) ≡ E(m).

cases.name: recognize-coherent-in-n
cases.note: The accepted base the refusals below are built from: set.json's recognize-coherent through E, spelled out. It adds no judgment, since set-json-recognize-through-embedding already carries it. It is here so that each refusal differs from it by exactly one visible change, and to fix the `bytes` member spelling: {"some": ""} is the empty byte string, the member at the empty key, and it coheres.

cases.name: recognize-valued-set-node
cases.note: New in N. The base with one change: the set node carries its own value. 0005: accepting it would read this node and the base, which differ only in the parent's own value, as the same set, so set identity would be coarser than node identity. It is not leaf_node, because the node has members: a check migrated as 'a value means a leaf' mislabels it. An implementation that inspects only the children accepts it. For the childless valued node, see the finding in set-json-recognize-through-embedding.

cases.name: recognize-valued-set-node-with-empty-value
cases.note: The same change, with the empty byte string as the set node's value. ADR 0009 §4: None differs from every Some(t), including a payload's own empty value. A presence check written as truthiness (`if own:`) reads Some("") as absent and accepts this node, which merges it with the base, a different node.

cases.name: recognize-member-with-children
cases.note: New in N. The base with one change: member 01 has one child, and that child is the empty node. Key 01 still equals e(member), so the child is the only defect. m ≠ ∅ holds although the child carries no value: ADR 0009 §4 distinguishes an existing node with None from an absent one. So a check for 'no values below a member' accepts this node, wrongly. It is not struct_member, because the member's own value is Some: a check migrated as 'children mean a struct' mislabels it.
